disease_mutation_base_rows.name: disease_mutation_base_rows
disease_mutation_base_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id AS id,
  dm.chromosome_id AS chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos AS chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt AS ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt AS alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id AS ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos AS cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos AS peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb AS aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa AS ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa AS alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq AS mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source AS data_source,
  dm.doid AS doid
FROM

disease_mutation_base_rows.description: Row-level cohort of disease_mutation records with all raw columns exposed. Use this as the canonical base for filters, joins, and further normalization.
validated_on: Show me all information about disease mutations with amino acid residue (ref_aa) equal to E
counter_examples: List all disease mutation chromosome positions data for disease skin cancer

disease_mutation_with_transcript_uniprot.name: disease_mutation_with_transcript_uniprot_map
disease_mutation_with_transcript_uniprot.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id,
  dm.chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt,
  -- prefer ensembl_transcript_id from disease_mutation; if null, fall back to mapping table
  COALESCE(dm.ensembl_transcript_id, m.ensembl_transcript_id) AS ensembl_transcript_id,
  m.uniprotkb_ac,
  dm.cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source,
  dm.doid
FROM
  disease_mutation AS dm
  LEFT JOIN map_protein_disease_mutation AS m
    ON dm.ensembl_transcript_id IS NOT NULL
       AND m.ensembl_transcript_id = dm.ensembl_transcript_id
disease_mutation_with_transcript_uniprot.description: Denormalized disease mutation rows joined to protein/transcript mapping (uniprot and ensembl transcript). One row per disease_mutation, including mapped peptide/protein identifiers where available.

disease_mutation_entity_context.name: disease_mutation_entity_context

  NULLIF(regexp_replace(btrim(coalesce(speciescommonname, '')), '\s+', ' ', 'g'), '') AS speciescommonname,

biomarker_edrn_by_phase.name: biomarker_edrn_by_phase
biomarker_edrn_by_phase.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  -- normalized title: trim whitespace, collapse internal multiple spaces to single space, NULL if empty after trim
  NULLIF(regexp_replace(trim(biomarker_title), '\s+', ' ', 'g'), '') AS biomarker_title,
  -- normalized QA state: lowercase, trim, NULL if empty
  NULLIF(lower(trim(qa_state)), '') AS qa_state,
  -- normalize phase: uppercase trim, canonicalize common representations (e.g., 'phase i' -> 'PHASE I', 'phase 1' -> 'PHASE I')
  NULLIF(
    regexp_replace(
      upper(trim(phase)),
      -- map numeric phases to roman numerals and normalize spacing: 'PHASE *1' -> 'PHASE I', 'PHASE I/II' kept
      '\bPHASE\s*([0-9]+)\b',
      -- replace numeric with roman (1->I,2->II,3->III,4->IV); fallback to captured if unmatched
      CASE
        WHEN regexp_replace(upper(trim(phase)), '\D', '', 'g') = '1' THEN 'PHASE I'
        WHEN regexp_replace(upper(trim(phase)), '\D', '', 'g') = '2' THEN 'PHASE II'
        WHEN regexp_replace(upper(trim(phase)), '\D', '', 'g') = '3' THEN 'PHASE III'
        WHEN regexp_replace(upper(trim(phase)), '\D', '', 'g') = '4' THEN 'PHASE IV'
        ELSE '\1'
      END,
      'g'
    ),
    ''
  ) AS phase
FROM biomarker_edrn
biomarker_edrn_by_phase.description: Normalized projection of biomarker_edrn focusing on phase, title and QA state; cleans/trims textual fields for consistent downstream filtering and comparisons.

biomarker_gene_canonical.name: biomarker_gene_canonical
biomarker_gene_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  -- Canonical gene symbol: nullify empty/whitespace, trim, upper-case for normalization
  -- Lift literal '' used to detect empty strings (trimmed) out of view logic if needed by callers
  (CASE
     WHEN b.gene_symbol IS NULL THEN NULL
     WHEN length(trim(b.gene_symbol)) = 0 THEN NULL
     ELSE upper(trim(b.gene_symbol))
   END) AS gene_symbol_canonical,
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol_original
FROM biomarker b
biomarker_gene_canonical.description: Normalized projection of biomarker -> canonical gene_symbol (trim/upper/NULL-cleaned). Exposes one row per biomarker id with a cleaned gene_symbol suitable for deduplication and joins.

biomarker_edrn_type_projection.name: biomarker_edrn_type_projection
biomarker_edrn_type_projection.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  NULLIF(trim(biomarker_title), '') AS biomarker_title,
  NULLIF(trim(biomarker_type), '') AS biomarker_type,
  -- canonicalize biomarker_type into a small controlled vocabulary.
  -- Lifted literals for mapping:
  --  'diagnostic', 'prognostic', 'predictive', 'monitoring', 'screening', 'pharmacodynamic', 'susceptibility'
  CASE
    WHEN lower(trim(coalesce(biomarker_type, ''))) IN ('diagnostic') THEN 'diagnostic'
    WHEN lower(trim(coalesce(biomarker_type, ''))) IN ('prognostic') THEN 'prognostic'
    WHEN lower(trim(coalesce(biomarker_type, ''))) IN ('predictive') THEN 'predictive'
    WHEN lower(trim(coalesce(biomarker_type, ''))) IN ('monitoring') THEN 'monitoring'
    WHEN lower(trim(coalesce(biomarker_type, ''))) IN ('screening') THEN 'screening'
    WHEN lower(trim(coalesce(biomarker_type, ''))) IN ('pharmacodynamic') THEN 'pharmacodynamic'
    WHEN lower(trim(coalesce(biomarker_type, ''))) IN ('susceptibility') THEN 'susceptibility'
    -- common variants / synonyms
    WHEN lower(trim(coalesce(biomarker_type, ''))) IN ('diagnostic test', 'diagnosis') THEN 'diagnostic'
    WHEN lower(trim(coalesce(biomarker_type, ''))) IN ('prognostic marker') THEN 'prognostic'
    WHEN lower(trim(coalesce(biomarker_type, ''))) IN ('predictive marker', 'predictor') THEN 'predictive'
    WHEN lower(trim(coalesce(biomarker_type, ''))) IN ('monitor', 'monitoring marker') THEN 'monitoring'
    WHEN lower(trim(coalesce(biomarker_type, ''))) IN ('screen', 'screening test') THEN 'screening'
    WHEN lower(trim(coalesce(biomarker_type, ''))) IN ('pharmacodynamic marker') THEN 'pharmacodynamic'
    WHEN lower(trim(coalesce(biomarker_type, ''))) IN ('risk', 'susceptibility marker') THEN 'susceptibility'
    -- fallback: normalize blanks to NULL, otherwise preserve trimmed original
    WHEN trim(coalesce(biomarker_type, '')) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE trim(biomarker_type)
  END AS biomarker_type_canonical,
  NULLIF(trim(qa_state), '') AS qa_state,
  NULLIF(trim(phase), '') AS phase,
  NULLIF(trim(uberon_anatomical_id), '') AS uberon_anatomical_id
FROM biomarker_edrn
biomarker_edrn_type_projection.description: Normalized projection of biomarker_edrn focusing on canonicalized biomarker_type and important descriptive fields; trims/standardizes empty strings to NULL for consistent downstream filtering.
counter_examples: Get all distinct biomarker EDRN phases

disease_mutation_mapped_genes.name: disease_mutation_mapped_genes
disease_mutation_mapped_genes.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id AS id,
  dm.doid AS doid,
  m.ensembl_transcript_id AS ensembl_transcript_id,
  m.uniprotkb_ac AS uniprotkb_ac,
  x.ensembl_gene_id AS ensembl_gene_id,
  x.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol
FROM disease_mutation dm
JOIN map_protein_disease_mutation m
  ON m.ensembl_transcript_id = dm.ensembl_transcript_id
LEFT JOIN map_uniprot_canonical_id u
  ON u.uniprotkb_ac = m.uniprotkb_ac
LEFT JOIN xref_gene_ensembl x
  ON x.ensembl_gene_id = m.ensembl_transcript_id
disease_mutation_mapped_genes.description: Mappings from disease mutations to gene identifiers and (where available) gene symbols via mapping tables. One row per disease_mutation id associated with a mapped ensembl_transcript_id and optionally mapped to a gene (xref_gene_ensembl).

biomarker_to_disease_cohort.name: biomarker_to_disease_cohort
biomarker_to_disease_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS biomarker_id,
  -- disease_id: prefer explicit mapped DOID when available, else NULL for a text-match-only association
  COALESCE(dm.doid, fda.doid, NULL) AS disease_id,
  -- association_source: origin of the association
  assoc.source AS association_source,
  -- match_field: which field produced the match (kept as literal lifted out of view)
  assoc.match_field AS match_field,
  -- match_text: the text that was matched or tag describing the association
  assoc.match_text AS match_text
FROM biomarker b
-- 1) Explicit join via biomarker_fda -> biomarker_fda_test which can carry a doid (FDA test indicates a disease)
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda bf ON bf.id = b.id
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda_test fda ON fda.test_trade_name = bf.test_trade_name AND fda.test_submission = bf.test_submission
-- 2) Disease-mutation based links: match on gene_symbol -> map to disease_mutation via ensembl/transcript if available.
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  -- Build a unioned set of possible associations (one row per source for this biomarker)
  SELECT
    'fda_test'::text AS source,
    'test_trade_name'::text AS match_field,
    fda.test_trade_name::text AS match_text,
    fda.doid::bigint AS doid
  WHERE fda.test_trade_name IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    'biomarker_alias'::text AS source,
    'alias'::text AS match_field,
    ba.alias::text AS match_text,
    NULL::bigint AS doid
  FROM biomarker_alias ba
  WHERE ba.biomarker_internal_id = b.id

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    'biomarker_article'::text AS source,
    'pmid'::text AS match_field,
    ba2.pmid::text AS match_text,
    NULL::bigint AS doid
  FROM biomarker_article ba2
  WHERE ba2.biomarker_internal_id = b.id

  UNION ALL

  -- heuristic: match biomarker.gene_symbol to disease_mutation. Try exact gene_symbol -> ensembl mapping via xref then disease_mutation with that ensembl_transcript_id
  SELECT
    'disease_mutation'::text AS source,
    'gene_symbol'::text AS match_field,
    dm2.doid::text AS match_text,
    dm2.doid::bigint AS doid
  FROM xref_gene_ensembl xge
  JOIN disease_mutation dm2 ON dm2.ensembl_transcript_id = xge.ensembl_gene_id
  WHERE xge.gene_symbol = b.gene_symbol

  UNION ALL

  -- fallback heuristic: direct textual match of biomarker_id or gene_symbol against disease.name (possible tag)
  SELECT
    'disease_name_text_match'::text AS source,
    'gene_symbol_or_biomarker_id'::text AS match_field,
    d.name::text AS match_text,
    d.id::bigint AS doid
  FROM disease d
  WHERE
    COALESCE(b.gene_symbol, '') <> ''
    AND position(lower(b.gene_symbol) in lower(d.name)) > 0

  UNION ALL

  -- heuristic: match biomarker_description text to disease.name (textual hint)
  SELECT
    'disease_name_text_match'::text AS source,
    'biomarker_description'::text AS match_field,
    d.name::text AS match_text,
    d.id::bigint AS doid
  FROM disease d
  WHERE
    COALESCE(b.biomarker_description, '') <> ''
    AND position(lower(d.name) in lower(b.biomarker_description)) > 0
) AS assoc ON TRUE

-- carry through any disease_mutation direct mapping if present (explicit table linking biomarkers to disease mutations isn't in schema;
-- use disease_mutation matching via gene_symbol or via mapped ensembl if possible)
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT dm.doid
  FROM disease_mutation dm
  WHERE
    -- try to match by amino-acid positions or gene symbol contexts: use ensembl_transcript_id match if gene_symbol maps to ensembl via xref
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM xref_gene_ensembl x WHERE x.gene_symbol = b.gene_symbol AND x.ensembl_gene_id = dm.ensembl_transcript_id
    )
  LIMIT 1
) dm ON TRUE

-- ensure one row per biomarker_id, association_source, take first match from assoc (postgres doesn't guarantee order, but this keeps grain)
GROUP BY b.id, COALESCE(dm.doid, fda.doid, NULL), assoc.source, assoc.match_field, assoc.match_text
biomarker_to_disease_cohort.description: Denormalized candidate associations between biomarkers and diseases derived from explicit join tables where present or from text-match heuristics on biomarker fields. Each row represents a possible link between a biomarker and a disease id (if known) or a text-match tag.

biomarker_edrn_phase_list.name: biomarker_edrn_phase_list
biomarker_edrn_phase_list.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(trim(phase), ''), '')::text AS phase_clean
FROM
  biomarker_edrn
biomarker_edrn_phase_list.description: Normalized projection of biomarker_edrn rows exposing the phase value (cleaned) per biomarker_edrn record. Use to list distinct phase values or filter biomarkers by phase. Trims whitespace and treats empty strings as NULL.

differential_expression_with_disease.name: differential_expression_with_disease
differential_expression_with_disease.body_sql:
SELECT
  de.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  de.doid AS doid,
  de.pvalue AS pvalue,
  d.name AS disease_name
FROM
  differential_expression de
LEFT JOIN
  disease d
ON
  de.doid = d.id
differential_expression_with_disease.description: Denormalized view joining differential_expression to disease, providing differential expression measures together with disease name for easy filtering by disease.name.

mutation_with_disease.name: mutation_with_disease
mutation_with_disease.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id AS id,
  dm.chromosome_id AS chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos AS chromosome_pos,
  dm.doid AS doid,
  d.id AS disease_id,
  d.name AS disease_name
FROM
  disease_mutation AS dm
LEFT JOIN
  disease AS d
ON
  dm.doid = d.id
mutation_with_disease.description: Denormalized join of disease_mutation to disease, producing one row per mutation annotated with its disease name to support disease-based cohort filtering (keeps chromosome location fields intact).

disease_by_name_tokens.name: disease_by_name_tokens
disease_by_name_tokens.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.id AS id,
  d.name AS name,
  lower(d.name) AS name_lower,
  -- lift token literals out: 'skin', 'cutaneous', 'melanoma'
  (lower(d.name) ~ ('\\m' || 'skin' || '\\M'))::boolean AS has_token_skin,
  (lower(d.name) ~ ('\\m' || 'cutaneous' || '\\M'))::boolean AS has_token_cutaneous,
  (lower(d.name) ~ ('\\m' || 'melanoma' || '\\M'))::boolean AS has_token_melanoma
FROM
  disease d
disease_by_name_tokens.description: Canonicalized disease table rows with lowercase name and token flags for common keywords. Facilitates text filtering/joining on disease names (e.g., 'skin', 'cutaneous', 'melanoma') without embedding literals in downstream views.

disease_mutation_with_disease.name: disease_mutation_with_disease
disease_mutation_with_disease.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id AS id,
  dm.chromosome_id AS chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos AS chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt AS ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt AS alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id AS ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos AS cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos AS peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb AS aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa AS ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa AS alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq AS mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source AS data_source,
  dm.doid AS doid,
  d.name AS disease_name
FROM
  disease_mutation dm
LEFT JOIN
  disease d
ON
  dm.doid = d.id
disease_mutation_with_disease.description: Denormalized rows joining disease_mutation to disease so queries can filter by disease.name or disease attributes alongside mutation fields. Keeps mutation grain (one row per mutation).

disease_mutation_prediction_annotations.name: disease_mutation_prediction_annotations
disease_mutation_prediction_annotations.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id AS id,
  dm.chromosome_id AS chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos AS chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt AS ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt AS alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id AS ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos AS cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos AS peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb AS aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa AS ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa AS alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq AS mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source AS data_source,
  dm.doid AS doid,
  dpi.id AS impact_prediction_id,
  dpi.site_prediction AS site_prediction,
  dpi.probability AS probability,
  dpi.tool AS tool,
  sa.id AS site_annotation_id,
  sa.description AS description,
  sa.feature_key AS feature_key
FROM
  disease_mutation dm
  LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_impact_prediction dpi
    ON dpi.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
  LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_site_annotation sa
    ON sa.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
disease_mutation_prediction_annotations.description: Per-mutation view that includes linked impact predictions and site annotations. One row per disease_mutation combined with a prediction or annotation row (many-to-many exploded).

fda_tests_row_level.name: fda_tests_row_level
fda_tests_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  test_trade_name,
  test_submission,
  test_manufacturer,
  test_approval_status,
  test_number_genes,
  clinical_significance
FROM
  biomarker_fda_test
fda_tests_row_level.description: Row-level cohort of FDA tests (one row per FDA test submission/trade name) exposing identity, manufacturer, submission id and other descriptive fields for filtering and counting.

biomarker_fda_test_with_fda.name: biomarker_fda_test_with_fda
biomarker_fda_test_with_fda.body_sql:
SELECT
  bf.id AS "biomarker_fda.id",
  ft.test_trade_name,
  ft.test_submission,
  ft.test_manufacturer,
  ft.biomarker_origin,
  ft.test_approval_status
FROM biomarker_fda bf
JOIN fda_tests_rowlevel ft
  ON (bf.test_trade_name = ft.test_trade_name OR bf.test_submission = ft.test_submission)
biomarker_fda_test_with_fda.description: Denormalized view joining FDA test details to biomarker_fda (linking test submissions to biomarker_fda id and trade name). Useful when queries need FDA test info alongside biomarker_fda identifiers or drug/NCIt mappings.

gene_differential_expression_with_diseas.name: gene_differential_expression_with_disease
gene_differential_expression_with_diseas.body_sql:
SELECT
  de.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  de.doid AS doid,
  d.name AS disease_name,
  de.log2fc AS log2fc,
  de.pvalue AS pvalue,
  de.adjpvalue AS adjpvalue,
  de.statistical_significance AS statistical_significance,
  de.expression_change_direction AS expression_change_direction,
  de.subjects_total AS subjects_total
FROM
  differential_expression de
LEFT JOIN
  disease d
ON
  de.doid = d.id
gene_differential_expression_with_diseas.description: Denormalized view joining differential expression rows to disease names. One row per gene_symbol + doid combination with associated disease.name, ready for filtering on gene and textual significance/direction.
validated_on: Show name of diseases where the gene expression with symbol A1BG has a statistical significance of 'Yes'

species_all_rows.name: species_all_rows
species_all_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  species.speciesid AS speciesid,
  species.genus AS genus,
  species.species AS species,
  species.speciescommonname AS speciescommonname
FROM
  species
species_all_rows.description: One-row-per-species exact projection of the species table (no filters). Useful as the canonical row-level cohort for any question that needs species attributes or counts.

species_projection_canonical.name: species_projection_canonical
species_projection_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  speciesid,
  trim(coalesce(genus::text, '')) AS genus,
  trim(coalesce(species::text, '')) AS species,
  trim(coalesce(speciescommonname::text, '')) AS speciescommonname
FROM
  species
species_projection_canonical.description: Normalized projection of species with explicit type-casting and canonical null handling for text fields. Keeps the same grain as the species table but ensures consistent string output and trims whitespace.

gene_symbol_to_ensembl_and_species.name: gene_symbol_to_ensembl_and_species
gene_symbol_to_ensembl_and_species.body_sql:
SELECT
  x.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  x.ensembl_gene_id AS ensembl_gene_id,
  x.speciesid AS speciesid
FROM xref_gene_ensembl x
WHERE x.ensembl_gene_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY x.gene_symbol, x.ensembl_gene_id, x.speciesid
gene_symbol_to_ensembl_and_species.description: Mapping of gene symbol to Ensembl gene id with species context (useful for linking expression and external resources). One row per ensembl_gene_id.
counter_examples: Show the pvalue of differential expression of lung cancer

differential_expression_rows.name: differential_expression_rows
differential_expression_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  gene_symbol,
  doid,
  log2fc,
  pvalue,
  adjpvalue,
  statistical_significance,
  expression_change_direction,
  subjects_up,
  subjects_down,
  subjects_nochange,
  subjects_nocoverage,
  subjects_total
FROM differential_expression
differential_expression_rows.description: Row-level differential expression results for each gene-disease pair (one row per gene_symbol + doid), exposing raw statistics and counts so downstream queries can filter by gene, disease, significance, etc.
validated_on: Show name of diseases where the gene expression with symbol A1BG has a statistical significance of 'Yes'

cancer_tissue_by_doid.name: cancer_tissue_by_doid
cancer_tissue_by_doid.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.doid AS doid,
  ct.uberon_anatomical_id AS uberon_anatomical_id
FROM
  cancer_tissue ct
cancer_tissue_by_doid.description: Mapping of disease ontology id (doid) to anatomical Uberon ids for cancer tissues (one row per doid). Helps relate disease concepts to anatomical context such as 'lung'.

disease_mutation_article_links.name: disease_mutation_article_links
disease_mutation_article_links.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id                                                                    AS "disease_mutation.id",
  dm.chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source,
  dm.doid,
  dma.pmid                                                               AS "disease_mutation_article.pmid"
FROM
  disease_mutation dm
  JOIN disease_mutation_article dma
    ON dma.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
disease_mutation_article_links.description: View linking disease_mutation rows to associated publication PMIDs (zero-to-many). One row per (disease_mutation, pmid) pair to support provenance, citation counts, and filtering by literature.

healthy_expression_by_developmental_stag.name: healthy_expression_by_developmental_stage
healthy_expression_by_developmental_stag.body_sql:
SELECT
  he.ensembl_gene_id,
  he.uberon_anatomical_id,
  he.uberon_developmental_id,
  s.name AS stage_name,
  he.expression_level_gene_relative,
  he.expression_level_anatomical_relative,
  he.call_quality,
  he.expression_rank_score,
  he.expression_score
FROM
  healthy_expression he
LEFT JOIN
  stage s
ON
  he.uberon_developmental_id = s.id
healthy_expression_by_developmental_stag.description: Denormalized healthy_expression rows annotated with developmental stage id and stage name by joining healthy_expression to stage on uberon_developmental_id = stage.id. Exposes one row per healthy_expression measurement with stage metadata to support cohort filtering by stage name.

healthy_expression_core_projection.name: healthy_expression_core_projection
healthy_expression_core_projection.body_sql:
SELECT
  ensembl_gene_id,
  uberon_anatomical_id,
  uberon_developmental_id,
  NULLIF(expression_level_gene_relative, '')::text AS expression_level_gene_relative,
  NULLIF(expression_level_anatomical_relative, '')::text AS expression_level_anatomical_relative,
  NULLIF(call_quality, '')::text AS call_quality,
  -- normalize numeric scores: keep numeric, cast to double precision; empty strings -> NULL
  CASE
    WHEN expression_rank_score IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN expression_rank_score::text = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE expression_rank_score::double precision
  END AS expression_rank_score,
  CASE
    WHEN expression_score IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN expression_score::text = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE expression_score::double precision
  END AS expression_score
FROM healthy_expression
healthy_expression_core_projection.description: Canonical projection of healthy_expression with stable keys and cleaned numeric measures. Casts numeric fields to consistent types and exposes core columns used for filtering, grouping, and aggregation.

differential_expression_significant_gene.name: differential_expression_significant_gene_disease_pairs
differential_expression_significant_gene.body_sql:
SELECT
  de.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  de.doid AS doid,
  de.statistical_significance AS statistical_significance,
  de.log2fc AS log2fc,
  de.adjpvalue AS adjpvalue,
  d.name AS disease_name
FROM
  differential_expression de
  LEFT JOIN disease d ON de.doid = d.id
WHERE
  de.statistical_significance IS NOT NULL
differential_expression_significant_gene.description: Denormalized view joining differential expression rows to disease names, restricted to rows with a non-null significance annotation (exposes the disease name alongside the measurement).

biomarker_row_level_53.name: biomarker_row_level_53
biomarker_row_level_53.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  b.biomarker_description AS biomarker_description,
  b.test_is_a_panel AS test_is_a_panel
FROM
  biomarker b
biomarker_row_level_53.description: Row-level canonical biomarker records exposing identifier, gene symbol, description, and panel flag. Useful as the base cohort for queries about biomarkers and filtering by panel status or other attributes.

biomarker_with_aliases.name: biomarker_with_aliases
biomarker_with_aliases.body_sql:
SELECT
  ba.biomarker_internal_id,
  ba.alias,
  b.biomarker_id,
  b.gene_symbol,
  b.biomarker_description,
  b.test_is_a_panel
FROM biomarker_alias ba
JOIN biomarker b
  ON ba.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
biomarker_with_aliases.description: Denormalized biomarker rows joined to their aliases (one row per biomarker alias). Useful for searches that should consider alias names alongside the primary gene_symbol or biomarker id.

fda_test_use_rows.name: fda_test_use_rows
fda_test_use_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  test_trade_name,
  test_submission,
  approved_indication,
  actual_use
FROM biomarker_fda_test_use
fda_test_use_rows.description: Row-level cohort of FDA test usage records from biomarker_fda_test_use. One row per biomarker_fda_test_use.id capturing the reported actual and approved uses for a specific test trade_name + submission.

fda_tests_canonical.name: fda_tests_canonical
fda_tests_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  test_trade_name,
  test_submission,
  test_manufacturer,
  biomarker_origin,
  test_approval_status,
  clinical_significance,
  test_number_genes,
  platform_method,
  specimen_type
FROM
  biomarker_fda_test
fda_tests_canonical.description: Canonical list of FDA test records from biomarker_fda_test with primary key (test_trade_name, test_submission). Normalizes key columns and exposes descriptive/test metadata relevant for filtering and display.

fda_test_use_with_test.name: fda_test_use_with_test
fda_test_use_with_test.body_sql:
SELECT
  tufu.id AS id,
  tufu.test_trade_name AS test_trade_name,
  tufu.test_submission AS test_submission,
  tufu.actual_use AS actual_use,
  tufu.approved_indication AS approved_indication,
  ft.test_manufacturer AS test_manufacturer,
  ft.test_approval_status AS test_approval_status,
  ft.platform_method AS platform_method,
  ft.specimen_type AS specimen_type,
  ft.clinical_significance AS clinical_significance
FROM
  biomarker_fda_test_use tufu
LEFT JOIN
  -- join to fda test metadata on the composite natural key (lifted literals: none)
  biomarker_fda_test ft
ON
  ( (tufu.test_trade_name IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ft.test_trade_name)
    AND (tufu.test_submission IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ft.test_submission) )
fda_test_use_with_test.description: Denormalized rows combining biomarker_fda_test_use and biomarker_fda_test on (test_trade_name, test_submission). One row per biomarker_fda_test_use.id enriched with the test's metadata.

biomarker_core_58.name: biomarker_core_58
biomarker_core_58.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  b.biomarker_id AS biomarker_id,
  b.test_is_a_panel AS test_is_a_panel
FROM
  biomarker b
WHERE
  b.id IS NOT NULL
biomarker_core_58.description: One row per biomarker capturing its primary identifiers and gene symbol; filters out rows where biomarker.id is NULL to ensure stable key.

biomarker_with_aliases_59.name: biomarker_with_aliases_59
biomarker_with_aliases_59.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.gene_symbol,
  ba.alias
FROM
  biomarker b
LEFT JOIN
  biomarker_alias ba
    ON ba.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
biomarker_with_aliases_59.description: Denormalized rows of biomarkers joined to their aliases; one row per biomarker alias mapping (keeps biomarker.id as the biomarker grain and biomarker_alias.alias as the alias variant). Useful for lookup of alternate names/symbols.

biomarker_article_links.name: biomarker_article_links
biomarker_article_links.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  ba.pmid AS pmid
FROM
  biomarker b
  JOIN biomarker_article ba ON ba.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
biomarker_article_links.description: Biomarkers with linked article PMIDs; one row per biomarker–article pair to support literature-based filtering and counts.

biomarker_edrn_by_type_and_phase.name: biomarker_edrn_by_type_and_phase
biomarker_edrn_by_type_and_phase.body_sql:
SELECT
  biomarker_type,
  phase,
  count(*) AS biomarker_count
FROM biomarker_edrn
GROUP BY
  biomarker_type,
  phase
biomarker_edrn_by_type_and_phase.description: Counts of EDRN biomarkers grouped by biomarker_type and phase. Useful for quick cohort sizing and top-type/phase breakdowns.

biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy.name: biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy
biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  b.qa_state AS qa_state,
  b.biomarker_title AS biomarker_title,
  b.biomarker_type AS biomarker_type,
  b.uberon_anatomical_id AS uberon_anatomical_id,
  a.name AS "anatomical_entity.name",
  a.description AS "anatomical_entity.description",
  b.phase AS phase
FROM
  biomarker_edrn b
LEFT JOIN
  anatomical_entity a
ON
  b.uberon_anatomical_id = a.id
biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy.description: Denormalized EDRN biomarkers joined to anatomical entity names and descriptions via uberon_anatomical_id, exposing anatomical context for biomarker records.
counter_examples: Get all distinct biomarker EDRN phases

biomarker_basic_normalized.name: biomarker_basic_normalized
biomarker_basic_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id AS id,
  -- lift literal column names out: biomarker_title comes from biomarker_edrn if present, else NULL
  edrn.biomarker_title AS biomarker_title,
  edrn.biomarker_type AS biomarker_type,
  -- biomarker_id is the external identifier on biomarker table (not the PK id)
  b.biomarker_id AS biomarker_id,
  -- gene_symbol from biomarker table when available
  b.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  b.test_is_a_panel AS test_is_a_panel
FROM biomarker b
LEFT JOIN biomarker_edrn edrn
  ON edrn.id = b.id
biomarker_basic_normalized.description: Normalized biomarker table that exposes primary identifiers, gene symbol (if available via biomarker table), title and flags; used to join EDRN records to biomarker core info.

anatomical_entity_lookup.name: anatomical_entity_lookup
anatomical_entity_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  at.uberon_anatomical_id AS id,
  ae.name AS name,
  ae.description AS description
FROM
  -- source table that links disease/cancer to anatomical uberon ids
  cancer_tissue at
LEFT JOIN
  -- anatomical entity lookup by uberon id
  anatomical_entity ae
ON
  ae.id = at.uberon_anatomical_id
anatomical_entity_lookup.description: Lookup table mapping uberon_anatomical_id to anatomical entity name/description to enable human-readable anatomy filters and labels.

biomarker_core_65.name: biomarker_core_65
biomarker_core_65.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id                                                                        AS "biomarker.id",
  NULLIF(trim(b.gene_symbol), '')                                              AS "biomarker.gene_symbol",
  NULLIF(trim(b.biomarker_description), '')                                    AS "biomarker.biomarker_description",
  NULLIF(trim(b.biomarker_id), '')                                             AS "biomarker.biomarker_id",
  b.test_is_a_panel                                                            AS "biomarker.test_is_a_panel"
FROM
  biomarker b
biomarker_core_65.description: Canonical biomarker rows with core identifier and descriptive fields normalized/cleaned for downstream joins and filters.

disease_core.name: disease_core
disease_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.id           AS "disease.id",
  d.name         AS "disease.name"
FROM
  disease d
disease_core.description: Canonical disease rows (id and name) for lookup of disease entities by name or id (DOID).

biomarker_phase_cohort.name: biomarker_phase_cohort
biomarker_phase_cohort.description: Cohort view of biomarker_edrn rows projecting only id and phase for use in phase-focused filtering and aggregation. Exposes one row per biomarker id and is suitable for deriving distinct phases or counting biomarkers by phase.

cancer_doid_uberon_mapping.name: cancer_doid_uberon_mapping
cancer_doid_uberon_mapping.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.doid AS doid,
  ct.uberon_anatomical_id AS uberon_anatomical_id
FROM
  cancer_tissue ct
WHERE
